title: Rías Baixas
description: Green, wet Galicia: crisp, saline Albariño from granite and the Atlantic.
L: Rías Baixas is in Galicia, Spain's north-west corner, on the Atlantic coast. It takes its name from the rías, flooded river valleys like fjords, that cut into the coast. Granite dominates the soils. It's green and lush, very different from the rest of Spain. The DO was created in 1988.

The climate is maritime: mild temperatures, high humidity and lots of rain, often 1,600 mm or more a year, among Spain's wettest regions. The main challenge is fungal disease. Growers use high pergolas, parras, on granite posts, to keep grapes away from damp ground and let air flow.
Why are Rías Baixas vines trained on high pergolas?
To let air circulate and reduce rot

Rías Baixas has five sub-zones. Val do Salnés, the coolest and most Atlantic, is Albariño's historic heart, around Cambados. O Rosal and Condado do Tea, along the Miño river on the Portuguese border, are warmer, and blend Albariño with Loureiro and Treixadura. Soutomaior and Ribeira do Ulla complete them.
Val do Salnés, O Rosal, Condado do Tea
Rías Baixas lies on Galicia's Atlantic coast, on granite
It's wet and mild, fighting rot with high pergolas
Val do Salnés is the cool heart; the Miño zones are warmer

Albariño is about 96% of Rías Baixas' vineyards. Its thick skins resist rot in the damp climate. It gives crisp, aromatic, dry whites with lemon, grapefruit, white peach, apricot and a saline, mineral edge. Wines labelled Rías Baixas Albariño must be 100% Albariño.

In O Rosal and Condado do Tea, Albariño may be blended with Loureiro, floral, Treixadura, rounder, and Caíño Blanco. Most Albariño is fermented in steel and bottled young. Some producers age it on its lees for months or years, adding texture and allowing it to age; a few use oak. Rías Baixas also allows a little red wine.
Match each term to Rías Baixas.
Albariño aged on its lees for a year or more shows how serious it can be: creamy, saline and able to age five years or more.
What must a Rías Baixas Albariño contain?
Albariño is about 96% of the vineyards
Its thick skins resist rot; it gives peach and salinity
Blends add Loureiro and Treixadura; lees ageing adds depth
Reading Rías Baixas and eating with it

Labels show Rías Baixas DO, sometimes a sub-zone like Val do Salnés, and the grape. Rías Baixas Albariño means 100% Albariño; Rías Baixas Salnés, Condado do Tea or Rosal may be blends. Barrica means oak-aged. Most wines are released young, within a year of harvest.

Albariño is Galicia's seafood wine: pulpo a la gallega, octopus with paprika and olive oil, mussels, clams, scallops, razor clams, oysters and grilled fish. Galicia's seafood is famous across Spain. Serve at 8 to 10 degrees. Cambados holds an Albariño festival every August.
Which Galician dish is a classic match for Albariño?
Octopus with paprika suits Albariño's acidity and salinity.
Across the Miño river, in Portugal, the same grape is called Alvarinho and makes the wines of Monção e Melgaço.
Most Rías Baixas Albariño is released young.
Yes, usually within a year of harvest.
